title: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) with Netskope Private Access — VPN Replacement
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (ZTNA app publishing + identity policy + VPN coexistence/cutover; higher risk to access).
Netskope console internals are deferred to Netskope's official documentation (no fabricated menus); authored at the correct architectural/procedural level.
hook: Replace the VPN — give users least-privilege access to private apps, not the whole network
problem: Legacy VPN hands a user the whole network and is slow, hard to scale, and a favorite attacker on-ramp. This solution replaces it with Zero Trust Network Access using Netskope Private Access — publish individual private applications, grant identity- and posture-based least-privilege access, and reach apps without exposing the network — with a staged coexistence-then-cutover migration off the VPN.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — how ZTNA / Netskope Private Access works, private app publishing, identity- and posture-based access, the difference from VPN, and the coexistence-then-cutover migration.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Netskope tenant + Private Access, publisher/connector placement, Entra ID identity, the Netskope client, app inventory, a pilot group) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: deploy publishers/connectors, define private apps and access policy, steer pilot users, validate access and posture, run VPN coexistence then cutover, then expand.
5 PowerShell scripts — ZTNA-readiness discovery, private-app access validation, an access and usage report, safe remediation of broken app access, and a ZTNA user-assignment group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: Replace the VPN with Zero Trust Network Access using Netskope Private Access — publish private apps, grant identity- and posture-based least-privilege access, and reach apps without exposing the network, via a staged cutover. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
